'''2003 DPC Chicago''' was the Chicago DPC Championship, a Star Wars CCG constructed tournament played on 12 April 2003 at Pastimes, 8478 Golf Road, Niles, Illinois, during the DeckTech Player's Challenge weekend of 11–13 April 2003. It was the first event of the Players Committee's DPC Championship Series, co-sponsored by DeckTech, and "the first DPC in the Midwest" since the inaugural DeckTech Player's Challenge in Normal, Illinois, which drew "80+ players".<ref name="pc-dpcchi">[https://web.archive.org/web/20030418001540/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/dpcchicago.htm DPC Goes Back to it's Roots; Next Stop is the Windy City!], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 18 April 2003.</ref> [[Andrew Howard]] directed it; the entry fee was $20.<ref name="pc-events03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20031009215036/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/events.htm 2003 Events], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 9 October 2003.</ref> [[Justin Desai]] won and $500; Desai and [[Brian Fred]] qualified for Day 2 of the [[2003 World Championship]].<ref name="pc-may03">[https://web.archive.org/web/20031229115404/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/Archives/may03archives.htm May 03 Updates: DPC Chicago Finalist's Decks Posted! (2 May 2003)], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 29 December 2003.</ref><ref name="pc-events03" />

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Original VS4]] (from the card pool legal on the event date)
* '''Site:''' Pastimes, 8478 Golf Road, Niles, Illinois<ref name="pc-dpcchi" />
* '''Tournament director:''' [[Andrew Howard]]<ref name="pc-events03" />
* '''Players:''' 25 (24 after one drop)<ref name="pcf-1296">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040323102139/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1296&amp Live Coverage UPDATE #3], Andrew Howard (12 April 2003), Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 23 March 2004.</ref><ref name="pcf-1297">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040131132742/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1297&amp Live Coverage UPDATE #4], Andrew Howard (12 April 2003), Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 31 January 2004.</ref>
* '''Dates:''' 12 April 2003

== Results ==

Besides the $500 cash prize for the champion and two byes into Day 2 of the World Championships, the prizes announced on 9 April 2003 included a cash prize for the highest-placing player rated under 1700 and the chance for the runner-up to design a virtual card.<ref name="pc-dpcchiupd">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/dpcchicagoupdate04092003.htm DPC Chicago Begins on Friday!], swccgpc.com (9 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040617171106/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/dpcchicagoupdate04092003.htm Internet Archive]</ref> The Players Committee posted the top 4 with their prizes.<ref name="pc-may03" />

{| class="wikitable"
! Place !! Player !! Prize
|-
| 1st || [[Justin Desai]] || $500
|-
| 2nd || [[Brian Fred]] || $220
|-
| 3rd || [[Brian Hunter]] || $120
|-
| 4th || [[Clint Hays]] || $60
|}

Players confirmed in advance included [[Brian Hunter]] (Colorado), [[Mike Gemme]] (New York), [[Justin Desai]] (Massachusetts), [[Jonny Chu|Jonathan Chu]] (New York), [[Clint Hays]] (Tennessee) and [[Brian Fred]] (Indiana), who was looking to defend his claim as "King of the Midwest".<ref name="pc-dpcchi" /> Fred and Hays issued an open challenge to anyone who wanted a game of Spades or Hearts.<ref name="pc-dpcchiupd" />

[[Andrew Howard]] opened "the first LIVE Coverage by the SWCCG Player's Committee" on the PC forums on 10 April 2003, calling the weekend "easily the best event to date by the PC".<ref name="pcf-1290-23801">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23801#23801 DPC Chicago Coverage begins NOW!], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212948/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23884%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Players Committee Advocate [[Eric Olson]] played in the main event, and everyone who beat him was promised a special prize.<ref name="pcf-1296-23859">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23859#23859 Live Coverage UPDATE #2], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625211749/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23865%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

Andrew Howard's live coverage on the PC forums reported that the event "Started with 25 players, less than the expected turnout".<ref name="pcf-1296" /><ref name="pcf-1297-23870">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23870#23870 Live Coverage UPDATE #3], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212539/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23882%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Many local players had not been able to get a ride to the event, but most of those who came were from out of state, many of them travelling hundreds of miles, and Howard called it "the most competition I've seen since Worlds last year".<ref name="pcf-1297-23870" /> In the featured matches, [[Jonny Chu|Jonathan Chu]] (Light Side, Throne Room Mains) beat [[Edmund Gray]] (Dark Side, "Brian Fred Senate") in round 1, and [[Clint Hays]] (Dark Side, Lightsaber Combat mains) beat [[Michael Raveling]] (Light Side, Senate) in round 2; the round 3 featured match paired Hays (Light Side, Throne Room Mains) with [[Justin Desai]] (Dark Side, "Origins winning Senate, updated").<ref name="pcf-1297-23870" /> In round 4 Desai (Light Side, Lightsaber Combat) beat [[Brian Hunter]] (Dark Side, MKOS Scum) at the top table, in a rematch from FreedomCon II, with a [[Worrt]] coming from under his Starting Effect dominating Hunter's aliens; [[Ryan Fojtik|Ryan Fojitk]], from Wisconsin, handed Hays his second loss; [[Brian Fred]] beat Eric Olson to stay undefeated in second place; and Edmund Gray beat [[Al Schaefer]] by 3 Force.<ref name="pcf-1299-23883">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23883#23883 Live Coverage UPDATE #4], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040131132845/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1299%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> After four rounds the top tables stood: Justin Desai 8 (+80), Brian Fred 8 (+53), [[Ryan Fojtik|Ryan Fojitk]] 6 (+62), [[Jonny Chu|Jonathan Chu]] 6 (+59), Brian Hunter 6 (+40) and [[Eric Olson]] 6.<ref name="pcf-1297" /><ref name="pcf-1299-23883" /> Round 5 paired Desai (Light Side, Lightsaber Combat) with Fred (Dark Side, Dark Deal), Fojitk (Light Side, QMC) with Chu (Dark Side, Lightsaber Combat mains) and Hunter (Light Side, Local Uprising (V) speeders) with Olson (Dark Side, Rops).<ref name="pcf-1299-23883" /> In the live coverage's poll of picks to win, Chu (7 votes) and Hunter (6 votes) led on the afternoon of 12 April; Desai had 1 vote.<ref name="pcf-1290-23884">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23884#23884 DPC Chicago Coverage begins NOW!], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625212948/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23884%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> After five rounds Desai was the only undefeated player; the decks seen included DS Senate and LS Lightsaber Combat (Desai, [[Mike Gemme]]), DS Combat and Throne Room Mains (Chu, [[Clint Hays]]), Local Uprising (V) speeders (Hunter, Fred), Dark Deal (Fred), MKOS Scum (Hunter), Rops and EBO (Olson), RTP (James Beyer), TIE Bombers ([[Frank Amador]]), WYS and Senate (Edmund Gray), and Watto and QMC (Fojitk).<ref name="pcf-1299">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040131132845/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1299&amp Live Coverage UPDATE #5], Andrew Howard (12 April 2003), Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 31 January 2004.</ref><ref name="pcf-1302-23893">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23893#23893 Live Coverage UPDATE #5], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625214828/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23900%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> By then Desai had beaten the players ranked 1st, 2nd and 7th in the world rankings: Chu, Hunter and Fred. Round 6 paired Desai (Dark Side, Senate) with Chu (Light Side, Throne Room Mains), Fred (Light Side, Local Uprising (V) speeders) with Hunter (Dark Side, MKOS Scum), [[Mike Gemme|Michael Gemme]] (Light Side, Lightsaber Combat) with James Beyer, and Olson (Light Side, Funkadelic EBO) with Hays (Dark Side, Lightsaber Combat mains). Only one player was on WYS, which Howard put down to Watto's domination of WYS at the [[2002 World Championship|Worlds]], and only one on Watto; the Dark Side Combat decks used [[Security Precautions (V)]], and the Throne Room Mains decks were similar to [[Brian Rippetoe]]'s Worlds deck.<ref name="pcf-1302-23893" /> Asked by [[Michael Pistone]], Howard said the Light Side Combat decks used no racing or [[Fire Extinguisher|fire extinguishers]].<ref name="pcf-1302-23897">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23897#23897 Live Coverage UPDATE #5], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625214828/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23900%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Desai then beat Chu, who dropped after losing to Gemme, and Fojitk, and was the only undefeated player going into the last round, where he played Frank Amador (Dark Side, TIE Bombers); the other last-round pairings included Gemme against Fred, Hunter against Fojitk, and Hays (Dark Side) against Jeff Desando (Light Side). Prizes were to be awarded after that round, before the final.<ref name="pcf-1303-23904">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23904#23904 Live Coverage UPDATE #6], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040618033055/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23940%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> A player posting as Sithborg finished 16th, having lost to Hunter and Chu.<ref name="pcf-1303-23924">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23924#23924 Live Coverage UPDATE #6], Sithborg, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040618033055/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23940%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> The Players Committee linked decklist PDFs for all eight top-4 decks; only Desai's Dark list has been preserved.<ref name="pc-may03" />

== Side events ==

The weekend schedule had a Star Wars CCG Classic Format event on Friday 11 April ($5, with free entry into the DPC Championship) and an SWCCG Team Tournament ($25) on Sunday, with uncut sheets for the winning team.<ref name="pc-dpcchi" /> DPC Chicago was billed as the kickoff of the Players Committee's new Professional tournament series, with events for Star Wars CCG, [[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game|Lord of the Rings TCG]] and Magi-Nation Duel: a Lord of the Rings Tower Booster Draft and a Lord of the Rings Sword Tournament on Friday, a Magi-Nation Duel DPC Master Series and a Lord of the Rings TCG Warm-Up on Saturday, and a Lord of the Rings DPC Master Series on Sunday.<ref name="pc-dpcchi" /> The Friday [[Classic]] event drew 6 players and was won undefeated by [[Jonny Chu|Jonathan Chu]] with SYCFA Brangus and Local Uprising (V) Ketwol.<ref name="pcf-1295">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040131131102/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=1295&amp Live Coverage UPDATE #1], Andrew Howard (11 April 2003), Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 31 January 2004.</ref><ref name="pcf-1295-23848">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23848#23848 Live Coverage UPDATE #1], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (11 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210814/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23848%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> The new Hoth (V) Objectives made "a good showing" in the Classic event, and by Friday evening many top Star Wars CCG players had arrived, including Brian Hunter, Brian Fred, Justin Desai, Clint Hays, Jonathan Chu and Mike Gemme.<ref name="pcf-1295-23848" /> The Lord of the Rings Sword Tournament drew 15 players and was cut to four rounds; Gustaf Olson won the Narsil replica, edging out Mike Gemme in a timed game.<ref name="pcf-1295-23848" /><ref name="pcf-1296-23859" />
